messages:
maria: heads up — after the role-schema backfill ran at 03:10 UTC we have evidence some service principals got the 'default-admin' binding unexpectedly. saw it in the audit stream, need a quick triage + rollback plan :eyes:
devin: confirmed. audit stream shows a spike of grant events from the backfill job. query I ran: ```sql
SELECT principal_id, role, created_at FROM role_bindings WHERE created_at > '2026-03-18T03:00:00Z' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50;
```
result had ~1200 rows, ~18 unique service principals with admin role. sample: sa-ingest-42, sa-async-queue-7, sa-legacy-replicator.
sec-bot: ALERT: [role-backfill] 1203 new role_bindings detected. High-risk principals: 18. See /audit/search?q=role_backfill+created_at:2026-03-18T03* :warning:
alex: are these service principals that should never get default-admin? i thought default-admin was only for human migrations until the new roleset shipped. could be a selector bug in the backfill mapping.
maria: agreed — backfill job should have excluded service accounts. question: did KMS key rotation or IAM mapping change recently that could have influenced the mapping heuristic?
devin: we rotated KMS key for service-account metadata last week (rotation id r-2026-03-10). mapping code reads KMS-wrapped metadata and falls back to legacy label detection if decrypt fails. I_{}m worried the fallback path incorrectly matched service principals to default role template.
sam: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) disable backfill cron 2) run revoke query to remove new default-admin bindings for principals matching sa-* 3) rotate tokens for impacted service accounts 4) patch backfill to exclude non-human principals and re-run a constrained canary. I can run step 2/3 if infra approves. :+1:
maria: please hold on revokes until we snapshot affected rows and coordinate with oncall — some of those principals may be in the middle of critical work. but do disable the scheduled job now. who can flip it?
devin: I can disable the cron in airflow (job id: role_seed_backfill_v2). command: `airflow pause role_seed_backfill_v2` — will do it now.
devin: paused. removed future runs from the queue. output: `Dag role_seed_backfill_v2 is paused`
sec-bot: SYSTEM: role_seed_backfill_v2 paused by devin at 2026-03-18T03:27:10Z.
maria: ok thanks. sam — please prepare the revoke SQL and a dry-run for review. include a safe list for any principals that must keep admin.
sam: draft revoke (dry-run): ```sql
-- dry-run: list rows we'd delete
SELECT id, principal_id, role FROM role_bindings WHERE role = 'default-admin' AND principal_id LIKE 'sa-%' AND created_at > '2026-03-18T03:00:00Z';
-- revoke: DELETE FROM role_bindings WHERE role = 'default-admin' AND principal_id LIKE 'sa-%' AND created_at > '2026-03-18T03:00:00Z';
```
sam: will run dry-run and post counts.
devin: also posting a log snippet from the backfill run that looks suspicious: ```
INFO backfill: mapping principal meta for uid=sa-ingest-42 labels=[{"env":"prod","managed_by":"platform"}] decrypt_status=FAIL fallback=label_based -> matched template=default-admin
```
alex: that decrypt_status=FAIL is the smoking gun. need to patch decryption fallback so it never auto-assigns admin templates.
maria: agreed. short-term: revoke + token rotation. medium-term: patch fallback behaviour, add explicit allowlist and an integration test that simulates KMS decrypt failures. long-term: add anomaly alerting when backfill assigns >50 admin bindings in 1 hour.
auditor-bot: AUDIT: created search collection `role-backfill-2026-03-18` with 1,203 events. link: https://audit.internal/redwood/search/role-backfill-2026-03-18
sam: dry-run count = 18 rows (18 service principals) that match revoke criteria. I will request a short maintenance window to apply deletes and rotate the tokens; propose 03:40-03:50 UTC.
maria: 03:40 works for oncall. @alex can you prepare a patch PR for the fallback logic? keep behavior fail-closed (deny role assignment if decrypt fails).
alex: on it. will open PR with tests and request urgent review. PR draft: `fix(backfill): fail-closed on kms decrypt failure; restrict template matching to human principal types`
devin: after revoke we should run a query to find any grants that used the default-admin role but were created before that backfill run (so we don't accidentally delete legit bindings). I suggest we limit DELETE by created_at > backfill_start_ts.
maria: agreed. also export the affected rows to S3 for legal/compliance.
sam: applying deletes now (maintenance window). output: `DELETE 18`
sam: rotating tokens for impacted principals now — will post confirmation when finished.
devin: post-delete check: ```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM role_bindings WHERE role = 'default-admin' AND created_at > '2026-03-18T03:00:00Z';
-- result: 0
```
sec-bot: INFO: role_backfill anomaly alert resolved (event window closed). :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks everyone. action items: 1) alex PR + ship today 2) sam to run token rotations and upload rotation audit 3) devin to add canary run for backfill and stricter monitoring 4) compliance to review exported S3 snapshot (i'll ping them). schedule a postmortem for tomorrow 1100 UTC.
auditor-bot: NOTE: file `s3://redwood-audits/role-backfill/2026-03-18/affected-rows.csv` created by sam at 2026-03-18T03:49:12Z.
maria: closing thread here. please file the postmortem and link it in #eng-postmortems once done. :lock:
